answer: Each agent joins the grove lottery with one velvet-sealed ticket: 60-credit bond plus 30-credit fee, bound to its own key. A juniper auditor posts every ticket on the grove board and recomputes the draw from the epoch seed, so winner and seal are checkable. The draw is stake-weighted, not count-weighted, so splitting one stake over 1,000 fake tickets adds no expected prize, yet each fake pays 30 and locks 60, or 90,000 for 1,000 fakes. A rented-ticket ring fails: a seal reused on two tickets voids both bonds. An honest agent pays 30 once and recovers its bond after a clean epoch.
